Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: floors-europe production game asset.
subject: Five European building-floor slabs stacked vertically in one sheet, straight-on with zero perspective, same width, same line weight. ROW 1 WEAK: plain plaster facade, exactly two square windows as simple thin-line rectangles, no other detail. ROW 2 MID: the same facade with evenly spaced horizontal brick joint lines and four arched-top windows. ROW 3 HARD: a dense grid of stone joint lines and six narrow vertical slit windows like embrasures. ROW 4 ROOF CAP: a zinc mansard roof with three dormers and two chimney pots sitting above a short stretch of wall, the whole roof fitting inside the row height. ROW 5 GROUND ENTRANCE: two panelled doors reached by a few short step lines, one square window flanking each side, and a single stringcourse band along the top.
style: Minimal line art. Thin, even-weight black ink strokes #1A1A20 with rounded caps, drawn with a slight hand-drawn wobble but never rough or sketchy. Flat warm ivory ground #F4F1E8, completely untextured. Only one accent color exists in this world: yellow #FFD200, and it appears only where the slot explicitly allows it. STRICTLY FLAT: flat vector-like fills, no shading, no ambient occlusion, no gradient, no texture noise, no bevel, no 3D render, no drop shadow, no photoreal. Every filled area is ONE solid value from edge to edge, with no lighting direction and no cast shadow anywhere in the image. Line is the only way depth is described. Remove a line wherever the drawing survives without it. Deadpan and quiet. Every fill is one flat value with no joint shading, no recess shadow, no window glow and no per-brick tonal variation. Joints and bricks are LINES, never separately tinted blocks.
composition: 810x1020 with five slabs of 810x204 stacked with NO gaps, NO margins and NO ground line anywhere. Full bleed: the slabs run edge to edge and each row tiles seamlessly left to right, so the left and right edges of a row must match up when repeated. Windows and doors sit fully inside their own row and never cross a row boundary.
color: Ink #1A1A20 outlines. Fills #C9C2B4 for row 1, #BCAA9C for row 2, #ABA69E for row 3, and #BCAA9C again for rows 4 and 5. These values are close on purpose: the rows must be told apart by window shape and line density in pure greyscale, never by hue. Zero yellow. Zero ivory #F4F1E8 anywhere in the sheet. Every fill stays clearly brighter than the ink.

prompts.editPrompt: Precise cleanup of this flat game floor atlas. Preserve EXACTLY all existing architectural line shapes, the five row subjects, and their order. Change ONLY the fills and row spacing: EVERY non-ink pixel within a row must be the same SINGLE FLAT COLOR, no texture, no per-brick variation, absolutely no gradient. Row 1 fill #C9C2B4. Row 2 fill #BCAA9C. Row 3 fill #ABA69E. Rows 4 and 5 fill #BCAA9C. Window interiors and roof negative spaces use their own row's same flat fill. Ink is #1A1A20. Exactly five equal-height rows, edge to edge, with the row boundaries at 20%,40%,60%,80% of the image height. Target canvas 810x1020 or same ratio.
